label: Expected end date
summary: The date on which the raid is expected to finish.
details: Vanilla shows it on the raid's map icon tooltip as the estimated completion, and in the raid window as the finishing date and as the time left from today.

label: Name
summary: The name of the raid, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading text of the raid window.

label: Progress
summary: How much progress the raid has made so far, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the raid progress tooltip as the first half of "progress / progress needed". GetProgressNeeded gives the amount at which the raid is done.

label: Progress needed
summary: How much progress the raid needs in total to finish, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the raid progress tooltip after the current progress (GetProgress).

label: Progress share
summary: The raid's progress as a fraction of what it needs, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla feeds it to progress bars: on the raid's map icon and in the raid window.

label: Raided province
summary: The province that is being raided.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the loot the raid will bring (the province's loot), and in the raid window to reach the province and, through the province's title, that title's holder.

label: Raiders against garrison
summary: A decimal number for how the raiding soldiers weigh up against the defending garrison.
details: Going by its name and its place in the raid window, it fills a bar that sits between the raiding army's soldier count and the garrison's count. The game does not say how the number is worked out.

label: Progress breakdown text
summary: A ready-made text that explains the raid's progress.
details: Vanilla adds it below the "progress / progress needed" line of the raid progress tooltip. The raid window's texts list a daily progress made of a base part and a part from the raiding soldiers, which this text likely shows; the input does not confirm that.

label: Is blocked
summary: Whether the raid is currently blocked and makes no progress.
details: Vanilla shows a "raid blocked" icon on the raid's map icon when it is true and shows a part of the raid window only when it is false. The game has a text saying a raid is blocked while the raiding army is in a battle; this function is not tied to that text in the input.

label: Raid itself
summary: The raid itself, to pass along to something else.
details: Vanilla passes it to the default raid click action on the map icon and in the outliner, what that action does is not shown. The game documents no return type.

label: Access raid intent itself
summary: A function on a raid intent that, going by its name, hands back the intent itself.
details: A raid intent is what a raiding army plans to do with its loot when it returns, and it can add modifiers while raiding. Vanilla never names this function on raid intents; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Description
summary: The raid intent's description text.
details: Vanilla shows it under the intent's name in the tooltips for a single intent and for changing a raiding army's intent.

label: Icon
summary: The raid intent's icon picture.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the army window, the military window and the raid intent selection window. The game documents no return type.

label: Index
summary: A whole number that, going by its name, is the raid intent's position in the list of intents.
details: Vanilla never names it on raid intents; other types' GetIndex lines are only a hint. The raid intents file notes that the first available intent becomes a character's default.

label: Key
summary: Going by its name, the raid intent's script key as text (such as `pillage_intent` or `raze_intent`).
details: Vanilla never names it on raid intents; on buildings GetKey shows the script key in debug texts, which is only a hint.

label: Name
summary: The raid intent's display name.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the raid intent tooltips and as the text of each choice in the raid intent selection window.

label: Has icon
summary: Going by its name, whether the raid intent has an icon.
details: Vanilla never names it on raid intents; similar functions on laws and situation phases hide an icon when there is none, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether the raid intent is a real, existing intent rather than an empty one.
details: Vanilla never names it on raid intents; elsewhere IsValid checks such as one on a government are used to show something only when it exists, which is only a hint.

label: Localized text
summary: A text the raid intent produces from one argument; going by its name, it looks up a localization key.
details: Vanilla never names it on raid intents, and the game documents nothing about the argument. A global Localize function that turns a key into game text is used elsewhere, which is only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by the name, the key to look up.

label: Raid intent itself
summary: The raid intent itself, to pass along or compare.
details: Vanilla passes it to the raid intent selection window to select or test an intent, and compares it with the intent of the selection window's entries (RaidIntentData.GetType) to mark which choice is pressed. The game documents no return type.

label: Access intent entry itself
summary: A function on a raid intent entry (one row of the raid intent choices) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf belongs to another type and is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Raid intent
summary: The raid intent that this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it in the raid intent selection window to mark the matching choice as pressed and to set it as the character's default raid intent when clicked. The game documents no return type.

label: Intent entry itself
summary: A function on a raid intent entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self after other things, such as Character.Self passed as an argument, belongs to other types and is only a hint.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the raid intent selection window (where a raid intent is picked) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Can pick intent
summary: Whether the given raid intent can be picked in the raid intent selection window.
details: Vanilla passes each listed intent to it and greys the choice out when it is false. GetCanPickIntentDesc gives the matching explanation text.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the raid intent selection window.
details: Vanilla puts it on several buttons of that window.

label: Army
summary: The army the raid intent selection window is about, going by its name and its use as the window's data source.
details: Vanilla uses it to give part of the raid intent selection window the army to show. The game documents no return type.

label: Pick condition text
summary: A text that explains whether, or why not, the given raid intent can be picked.
details: Vanilla adds it as a paragraph to the tooltip for changing a raiding army's intent.

label: Character
summary: The character the raid intent selection window is about, going by its name and its use as the window's data source.
details: The same window can set a character's default raid intent, which fits this. The game documents no return type.

label: Possible raid intents
summary: The list of raid intents the window offers to choose from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that fills the choices of the raid intent selection window. The game documents no return type.

label: Selected raid intent
summary: The raid intent currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a part of the raid intent selection window, likely the part that shows the chosen intent. The game documents no return type.

label: Is for an army
summary: Whether the raid intent selection window was opened for an army rather than for something else.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla shows one set of parts when it is true and another when it is false. The same window can also set a character's default intent, which is likely the other case.

label: Select intent
summary: Selects the given raid intent in the raid intent selection window.
details: Vanilla calls it when one of the intent choices is clicked.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the raid intent selection window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window. Self on other types, such as Character.Self, is only a hint.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the raid window (the window about one ongoing raid) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on the raid window; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the raid window.
details: Vanilla puts it on the raid window's close button.

label: Raid
summary: The raid the raid window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the window's data source, so the raid's name, progress and province can be shown.

label: Open army window
summary: Opens the army window, going by its name; vanilla puts it on a button in the raid window.
details: The input does not show which army it opens; going by the window, likely the raiding army.

label: Open holding view
summary: Opens the holding view, going by its name; vanilla puts it on a button in the raid window.
details: Going by the window, it likely opens the view of the raided holding; the input does not say so directly.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the raid window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on the raid window; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access rally point itself
summary: A function on a rally point (a place on the map where a ruler's armies gather when raised) that, going by its name, hands back the rally point itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on rally points; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Color
summary: The rally point's color, as a four-number color value.
details: Vanilla tints parts of the military window and the rally point window with it.

label: Icon color
summary: The color used for the rally point's map icon, as a color value.
details: Vanilla tints the rally point icon on the map with it. GetColor is the color used in the windows.

label: Name
summary: The rally point's name.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the rally point's map tooltip.

label: Province
summary: The province where the rally point lies, going by its name and its return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on rally points; GetProvince on holdings, which leads to the holding's province, is only a hint.

label: Rally point itself
summary: A function on a rally point that hands back the rally point itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on rally points; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access entry itself
summary: A function on a rally point entry (one rally point in the military window's list) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Rally point
summary: The rally point this entry of the military window stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the rally point's name in the entry's tooltip and as the data source of the entry. The game documents no return type.

label: Click entry
summary: Does what clicking a rally point entry in the military window does.
details: Vanilla puts it on the entry's buttons; the entry's tooltip says to click to select, so it likely selects the rally point.

label: Entry itself
summary: A function on a rally point entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access map icon itself
summary: A function on a rally point's map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Can be clicked
summary: Whether the rally point's map icon reacts to clicks right now.
details: When it is false, vanilla lets clicks pass through the icon to the map. A comment in vanilla says this is for when a rally point is being moved or placed.

label: Rally point
summary: The rally point this map icon belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the icon on the map icon layer. The game documents no return type.

label: Click icon
summary: Does what clicking a rally point's map icon does.
details: Vanilla puts it on the icon's click action; the rally point tooltip says to click to view, so it likely opens the rally point.

label: Map icon itself
summary: A function on a rally point's map icon that hands back the icon itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Should be shown
summary: Whether the rally point's map icon should be shown.
details: Vanilla shows the icon only when this is true and the player has not handed raising armies to the AI helper (the companion setting for raising armies).

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the rally point window (the window of a selected rally point) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Can move rally point
summary: Whether the selected rally point can be moved now.
details: Vanilla greys out the window's move button when it is false. The button's tooltip notes the rally point can also be moved by right-clicking on the map.

label: Can raise local army
summary: Whether the "Raise Local Army" button of the rally point window can be used.
details: That button raises the armies closest to this rally point. Vanilla greys it out when this is false; GetRaiseTooltip gives the matching tooltip.

label: Can raise all here
summary: Whether the "Raise All Here" button of the rally point window can be used.
details: That button raises all the ruler's armies at this rally point, whichever rally point is closest to them. Vanilla greys it out when this is false.

label: Can raise barterers
summary: Whether the "Raise Local Barterers" button of the rally point window can be used.
details: That button raises the armies closest to this rally point as barter armies. Vanilla shows the button only when the player has barter goods and greys it out when this is false.

label: Can raise men-at-arms
summary: Whether the "Raise All Men-at-Arms Here" button of the rally point window can be used.
details: That button raises all men-at-arms (the ruler's professional regiments) at this rally point. Vanilla greys it out when this is false.

label: Can raise raiders
summary: Whether the "Raise Local Raiders" button of the rally point window can be used.
details: That button raises the armies closest to this rally point as raiding armies. Vanilla shows it only to a player who can raid and greys it out when this is false; the game's texts say raiders cannot be raised while at war.

label: Can remove rally point
summary: Whether the selected rally point can be removed.
details: Vanilla greys out the window's remove button when it is false; GetRemoveTooltip gives the matching tooltip.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the rally point window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window; it uses CloseAndDeselect instead, which also clears the selection.

label: Close and deselect
summary: Closes the rally point window and deselects the rally point.
details: Vanilla puts it on the window's close button.

label: Living local levies
summary: How many of the local levies are alive, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the local levies tooltip next to the unraised and total counts.

label: All troops summary
summary: The make-up of all the ruler's troops, shown in the rally point window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the "all soldiers" part of the window, with lines for levies, men-at-arms and knights. The game documents no return type.

label: Move button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the rally point window's move button.
details: The game's own text for it says to move the rally point, or to right-click on the map instead.

label: Raise all button tooltip
summary: Going by its name, a tooltip text for a "raise all" button of the rally point window.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the window uses GetRaiseAllTooltip for its "Raise All Here" button.

label: Raise all tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the "Raise All Here" button.
details: The game's texts for it explain that all armies are raised here, whichever rally point is closest to them.

label: Raise barterers tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the "Raise Local Barterers" button.
details: The game's texts for it list what blocks raising barterers, say barter armies cost a share of a normal army's upkeep and cannot reinforce.

label: Raise men-at-arms tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the "Raise All Men-at-Arms Here" button.

label: Raise raiders tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the "Raise Local Raiders" button.
details: The game's texts for it list what blocks raising raiders, say raid armies cost a share of a normal army's upkeep and cannot reinforce.

label: Raise local army tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the "Raise Local Army" button.
details: The game's texts for it explain that the armies closest to this rally point are raised, and that with only one rally point all armies are raised there.

label: Levy count text
summary: Going by its name, a text with the number of levies at the rally point.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so the input shows nothing more.

label: Local levies bar size
summary: The size of the local levies bar in the rally point window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the size of a progress bar for the local levies; going by its name, it scales with how large the local levies are compared with something else. The game documents no return type.

label: Remove button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the rally point window's remove button.

label: Selected rally point
summary: The rally point currently selected and shown in the window.
details: Vanilla shows its name as the window's heading and uses it as the data source of parts of the window. The game documents no return type.

label: Selected rally point entries
summary: A list of entries for the selected rally point, going by its name.
details: Vanilla fills a list with it and shows a part of the window only when the list has more than one entry. The input does not show what each entry is. The game documents no return type.

label: Time to raise
summary: Going by its name, a text with how long raising troops at the rally point takes.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window. A similar function on banner entries is shown as a number of days, which is only a hint.

label: Total local levies
summary: The total number of local levies for this rally point, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the local levies tooltip and uses it as the top value of the local levies bar.

label: Unraised local levies
summary: How many of the local levies are not raised yet, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number, in the local levies tooltip, and as the filled part of the local levies bar.

label: Move rally point
summary: Starts moving the selected rally point.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's move button, which is greyed out when CanMoveRallyPoint is false.

label: Raise local army
summary: Raises the armies closest to this rally point there.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Raise Local Army" button. With only one rally point, all armies are raised there.

label: Raise all here
summary: Raises all the ruler's armies at this rally point.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Raise All Here" button; it ignores which rally point is closest to each army.

label: Raise barterers
summary: Raises the armies closest to this rally point as barter armies.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Raise Local Barterers" button. Barter armies cost a set share of a normal army's upkeep and cannot reinforce.

label: Raise men-at-arms
summary: Raises all the ruler's men-at-arms at this rally point.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Raise All Men-at-Arms Here" button.

label: Raise raiders
summary: Raises the armies closest to this rally point as raiding armies.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Raise Local Raiders" button. Raid armies cost a set share of a normal army's upkeep and cannot reinforce.

label: Remove rally point
summary: Removes the selected rally point.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's remove button, which is greyed out when CanRemove is false.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the rally point window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access value itself
summary: A function on a randomizable decimal value that, going by its name, hands back the value itself.
details: Vanilla never names this type at all, so what such a value is used for is not shown. PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Value
summary: The current decimal number held by a randomizable value.
details: Going by its name and return type only; vanilla never names this type.

label: Randomize
summary: Going by its name, gives the decimal value a new random number.
details: Vanilla never names this type; the coat of arms designer's "Randomize" texts are a different thing and only a hint.

label: Value itself
summary: A function on a randomizable decimal value that hands back the value itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names this type.

label: Set value
summary: Going by its name, sets the decimal number of a randomizable value.
details: The game lists it with no arguments, so how the new number is given is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Access value itself
summary: A function on a randomizable whole-number value that, going by its name, hands back the value itself.
details: Vanilla never names this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Value
summary: The current whole number held by a randomizable value.
details: Going by its name and return type only; vanilla never names this type.

label: Randomize
summary: Going by its name, gives the whole-number value a new random number.
details: Vanilla never names this type; other "Randomize" texts in the game are only a hint.

label: Value itself
summary: A function on a randomizable whole-number value that hands back the value itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names this type.

label: Set value
summary: Going by its name, sets the whole number of a randomizable value.
details: The game lists it with no arguments, so how the new number is given is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Access entry itself
summary: A function on a ranked house entry (one house in the powerful families ranking of the administration window) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: House
summary: The dynasty house this ranking entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the entry in the government administration window. The game documents no return type.

label: Rank
summary: The house's place in the powerful families ranking, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the administration window and in a tooltip saying the house has that place in powerful family rating within the player's realm.

label: Is player's house
summary: Whether this ranking entry is the player's own house.
details: Vanilla shows the player's house larger in the ranking and shows or hides parts of the entry with it.

label: Entry itself
summary: A function on a ranked house entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access entry itself
summary: A function on a ranked royal court entry (one court in the grandest royal courts list of the languages window) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Court owner
summary: The character whose royal court this ranking entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of each entry in the grandest royal courts list of the languages window. The game documents no return type.

label: Rank
summary: The court's place in the grandest royal courts list, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as text on each entry of that list in the languages window.

label: Entry itself
summary: A function on a ranked royal court entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access reason itself
summary: A function on an event option reason (one icon next to an event option that shows why it is offered) that, going by its name, hands back the reason itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Skill
summary: The skill behind this event option reason.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the skill's icon next to the option when the reason is a skill (IsSkill), in letter and scheme preparation event windows. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait
summary: The trait behind this event option reason.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the trait's icon next to the option when the reason is a trait (IsTrait), in letter and scheme preparation event windows. The game documents no return type.

label: Is reason flag
summary: Whether this event option reason is the given named flag.
details: Vanilla checks it to choose the icon to show next to an event option, for flags such as `dread`, `activity_intent`, `prestige_level`, `piety_level` and `faith`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the flag to compare with.
fields.values: a quoted name, such as 'dread' or 'faith'

label: Is skill
summary: Whether this event option reason is a skill.
details: Vanilla shows the skill icon from GetSkillItem only when it is true.

label: Is trait
summary: Whether this event option reason is a trait.
details: Vanilla shows the trait icon from GetTrait only when it is true.

label: Reason itself
summary: A function on an event option reason that hands back the reason itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Access command itself
summary: A function on a recorded command that, going by its name, hands back the command itself.
details: Vanilla never names this type, so what a recorded command is, is not shown. PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Command payload
summary: The contents (payload) of a command recorded by the engine's session recorder, as text.
details: The session recorder (a debug tool that records game commands) shows it in the detail view of the selected command. What the text holds is not documented.

label: Command name
summary: The token (going by its use, the name) of a command recorded by the engine's session recorder, as text.
details: The session recorder (a debug tool that records game commands) shows it for each entry of its list of recorded commands and as the heading of the selected command.

label: Command itself
summary: A function on a recorded command that hands back the command itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names this type.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the reforge artifact window (where an artifact is reforged) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the reforge artifact window.
details: Vanilla puts it on that window's close button.

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact being reforged in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of several parts of the reforge artifact window. The game documents no return type.

label: Effects on artifact text
summary: A text describing what reforging does to the artifact, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the reforge artifact window.

label: Character
summary: The character who does the reforging in the window.
details: Vanilla passes it to the artifact's reforge check and reforge tooltip, to show and enable the reforge button. The game documents no return type.

label: Effects on character text
summary: A text describing what reforging does to the character, going by its name, such as its cost.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the reforge artifact window. That it includes the cost is a guess from the name and is not confirmed by the input.

label: Complete reforge text
summary: A text describing the complete reforge option, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the reforge artifact window; IsCompleteReforge tells whether that option is chosen.

label: Is complete reforge
summary: Whether the complete reforge option is ticked in the reforge artifact window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the tick box's state and to show different parts of the window for each choice. ToggleCompleteReforge switches it.

label: Reforge
summary: Reforges the artifact shown in the window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's reforge buttons, which are shown and enabled only when the artifact can be reforged by the window's character.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the reforge artifact window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this window; Self lines on other types are only a hint.

label: Toggle complete reforge
summary: Switches the complete reforge option on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it when the tick box is clicked; IsCompleteReforge reads the current state.

label: Access regiment itself
summary: A function on a regiment (a men-at-arms unit) that, going by its name, hands back the regiment itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on regiments; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Soldier count text
summary: A ready-made text with the regiment's current count, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it in the men-at-arms window, the military window and a tooltip. The input does not show the text's exact form.

label: Days to full strength
summary: Going by its name, how many days the regiment needs to reach full strength, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Months to full strength
summary: Going by its name, how many months the regiment needs to reach full strength, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Monthly upkeep
summary: The regiment's current upkeep cost, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as an amount per month in the men-at-arms view.

label: Maximum size
summary: The largest size the men-at-arms regiment can have, as a whole number of size steps.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Size current/maximum" and shows the size increase only when the current size (GetMAAChunkCount) is below it.

label: Living soldiers
summary: Going by its name, how many of the regiment's soldiers are alive, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Soldiers
summary: Going by its name, how many soldiers the regiment has, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Full upkeep
summary: The regiment's full monthly maintenance cost, as text.
details: Despite the name, vanilla labels this amount "Full Maintenance" per month, highlighted when the regiment is raised or below full strength, next to the cheaper unraised upkeep (CalcUnraisedCost).

label: Unraised upkeep
summary: The regiment's monthly cost while it is not raised, as text.
details: Vanilla labels it "Unraised Maintenance" per month and highlights it when the regiment is at full strength and not raised.

label: Unraised soldiers
summary: Going by its name, how many of the regiment's soldiers are not raised, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Army
summary: The army the regiment is currently in.
details: Vanilla shows that army's name in the men-at-arms view ("In Army: ..."). The game documents no return type.

label: Controlling title
summary: The title that currently controls the regiment.
details: When it differs from the owning title, vanilla's military window marks the regiment as "Loaned" and shows the controlling title's coat of arms. The game documents no return type.

label: ID
summary: The regiment's id number.
details: Vanilla passes it to open the men-at-arms view for this regiment from the county view.

label: Size
summary: The men-at-arms regiment's current size, as a whole number of size steps.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Size current/maximum" and in the texts for increasing or decreasing the size by one step.

label: Men-at-arms tooltip
summary: Going by its name, a tooltip text about the men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Men-at-arms type
summary: The regiment's men-at-arms type (such as a kind of infantry or cavalry).
details: Vanilla uses it to show the type's base name, its icon and its stack size next to the icon in the size change text. The game documents no return type.

label: Maximum soldiers
summary: Going by its name, the most soldiers the regiment can have, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never names it on regiments; a GetMaxCount on the levy view shown as "living/maximum" is only a hint.
